member_findings.reasoning: Hypothesis: any authenticated user can call `admin-ajax.php?action=backwpup_debug_info` and read the plugin's debug report because the AJAX callback in `inc/class-admin.php:281-290` has no `check_ajax_referer()` or `current_user_can()` gate. Trace: the closure calls `BackWPup_Page_Settings::get_information()` and then echoes every collected label/value pair back to the requester at `inc/class-admin.php:284-289`. `get_information()` assembles environment details such as the WP-Cron URL (`inc/class-page-settings.php:109-111`), server self-connect response details (`inc/class-page-settings.php:117-168`), the document root (`inc/class-page-settings.php:175-178`), temp/log folder paths (`inc/class-page-settings.php:180-215`), the current PHP user (`inc/class-page-settings.php:232-238`), and loaded PHP extensions (`inc/class-page-settings.php:346-352`). Defenses analyzed: output is wrapped in `esc_html()`, so this path is not an XSS sink, and the feature is clearly intended as privileged support/debug output. REFUTATION ATTEMPT: I looked for a shared nonce/capability check in this closure or in the surrounding AJAX registration path and found none before the response is sent. Conclusion: this is a real authenticated information disclosure to any logged-in user, not just users allowed to access BackWPup settings/support data.

phase3_review.reason: The wp_ajax_backwpup_debug_info closure at inc/class-admin.php:281-291 has no current_user_can() or check_ajax_referer() guard before calling BackWPup_Page_Settings::get_information() and echoing the results. The wp_ajax_ prefix requires WordPress login but imposes no capability filter, so any authenticated user including a plain subscriber with no BackWPup roles can obtain the full debug report containing DOCUMENT_ROOT, temp/log folder absolute paths, PHP user, server self-connect response, and loaded PHP extensions. The guard_contradiction issue in the gate is a false positive: there genuinely is no guard. The finding is consistent.

member_findings.review_reason:
inc/class-destination-downloader.php coverage gap: the file is reached via 'wp_ajax_download_backup_file' registered at inc/class-admin.php:296 calling BackWPup_Destination_Downloader::download_by_ajax(). The static download_by_ajax() method (lines 58-100) accepts $_GET['destination'], $_GET['jobid'], $_GET['file'], $_GET['local_file'] and passes them to $dest_class->file_download() with only sanitize_text_field() applied — no capability check, no nonce verification. By contrast, download_by_chunks() (line 109) does call $this->ensure_user_can_download() at line 110. The static download_by_ajax() method is missing both checks. 

However: this endpoint uses 'wp_ajax_' prefix (not 'wp_ajax_nopriv_'), so WordPress already requires the user to be logged in. The missing check is therefore capability escalation (any logged-in user, not just those with backwpup_backups_download capability) rather than unauthenticated access. The $dest parameter is used to call BackWPup::get_destination($dest) which returns a registered destination class — if $dest is an unexpected value, get_destination() behavior needs to be verified. The $file and $file_local parameters are sanitized with sanitize_text_field() but used in file_download() — the behavior of file_download() with attacker-controlled file paths is unknown from this file alone.

Resolution path: (1) Verify whether wp_ajax_download_backup_file allows any logged-in subscriber or requires higher capability — if any authenticated user can trigger this, it is a privilege escalation. (2) Trace $dest_class->file_download($job_id, $file, $file_local) to determine if the $file/$file_local parameters can be used for path traversal or SSRF. (3) Verify if there is a nonce passed in the AJAX call from the frontend that is not checked server-side.
member_findings.poc_description: Logged-in user (subscriber+) sends: POST /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?action=download_backup_file&destination=FOLDER&jobid=1&file=../wp-config.php&local_file=../wp-config.php. If file_download() follows these paths without further restriction, sensitive files may be disclosed.
member_findings.remediation: Add current_user_can(self::CAPABILITY) check and nonce verification at the start of download_by_ajax() before any processing, mirroring the ensure_user_can_download() guard in download_by_chunks().

The actual violation is missing capability check: download_by_ajax() at inc/class-destination-downloader.php:58 does not call ensure_user_can_download(), while download_by_chunks() at line 109 does call it at line 110. Any logged-in WordPress user (plain subscriber, no BackWPup roles) can trigger this and download backup archives. Gate code_evidence=1.0 and file_exists=1.0 confirm the file and sink. member_findings.reasoning: Hypothesis: a low-privileged BackWPup role can modify onboarding backup jobs through `admin-post.php?action=backwpup` even though that role does not have job-edit or settings privileges. Trace: `BackWPup_Admin::save_post_form()` only checks the page nonce and `current_user_can('backwpup')` at `inc/class-admin.php:838-852`. When `$_POST['page'] === 'backwpup'` and `$_POST['onboarding'] === '1'`, it dispatches directly into `BackWPup_Page_Onboarding::save_post_form()` at `inc/class-admin.php:892-895`. The onboarding UI is reachable while `backwpup_onboarding` is true through a submenu that requires only `backwpup_backups` (`inc/class-admin.php:658-667`), and its form posts a `backwpup_page` nonce plus hidden `onboarding=1` to `admin-post.php` (`plugins/backwpup/pages/onboarding.php:14-20`, `plugins/backwpup/components/containers/form-start.php:40-46`). Inside `BackWPup_Page_Onboarding::save_post_form()`, there is no capability re-check; it updates job options (`inc/class-page-onboarding.php:119-148`, `inc/class-page-onboarding.php:170-171`), schedules cron events (`inc/class-page-onboarding.php:140-146`), and flips the onboarding state (`inc/class-page-onboarding.php:173-175`). Defenses analyzed: the shared handler is partially safe for other branches because edit-job re-checks `backwpup_jobs_edit` (`inc/class-page-editjob.php:44-49`) and settings re-checks `backwpup_settings` (`inc/class-page-settings.php:417-420`). REFUTATION ATTEMPT: I tried to disprove exploitability by finding an equivalent second capability check in the onboarding branch; none exists. The bundled `backwpup_check` role explicitly has `backwpup` and `backwpup_backups` but lacks `backwpup_jobs_edit` and `backwpup_settings` (`inc/class-install.php:142-158`), so the weaker top-level gate is materially broader than the intended privilege boundary. Conclusion: while onboarding is active, a low-privileged BackWPup role can alter backup scheduling/destination state beyond its assigned permissions.
member_findings.poc_description: Assign a user the `backwpup_check` role while `backwpup_onboarding` is still enabled. Visit the onboarding page to obtain the `backwpup_page` nonce, then submit `POST /wp-admin/admin-post.php` with `action=backwpup`, `page=backwpup`, `onboarding=1`, chosen frequency fields, and `onboarding_storage[]`. The request updates onboarding job options and marks onboarding complete even though the role lacks `backwpup_jobs_edit` and `backwpup_settings`.
member_findings.remediation: Require a stronger capability such as `backwpup_jobs_edit` or `backwpup_settings` before calling `BackWPup_Page_Onboarding::save_post_form()`.

phase3_review.reason: The shared save_post_form() handler at inc/class-admin.php:838-852 checks check_admin_referer(._page) and current_user_can(backwpup) — not backwpup_jobs_edit. When onboarding===1, it delegates to BackWPup_Page_Onboarding::save_post_form() at line 892-895 without any secondary capability check. The backwpup_check role (backwpup=true, backwpup_jobs_edit=false) can access the onboarding submenu (inc/class-admin.php:658-667 requires only backwpup_backups) and thus obtain the backwpup_page nonce. The BAC violation is that the onboarding branch bypasses the job-edit check that all other job-mutating branches enforce.

counter_evidence.detail: Page allowlist restricts dispatch to known pages.
check_admin_referer(._page) requires valid page-scoped nonce — CSRF blocked without it.

missing_evidence: Confirm the onboarding submenu renders a form with the backwpup_page nonce for backwpup_check users.
